units.title: Electrostatics and electric fields
units.why: Electric fields explain forces between charges and energy transfer in technology.
principles: like charges repel and unlike charges attract
field direction is force on a positive test charge
examples: Doubling separation reduces Coulomb force by factor four
Field lines are denser where field magnitude is greater
practice: Why field lines do not cross?

videoPackage.title: Seeing electric fields
videoPackage.transcript: We define field direction using a positive test charge, compare charge interactions, and read field diagrams without treating lines as tracks.

units.title: Electric circuits and power
units.why: Circuit analysis supports safe electrical design and energy efficiency.
principles: series current is common; parallel potential difference is common
examples: 12 V across 4 Ω gives I=3 A and P=36 W
Two equal resistors in series double total resistance
misconceptions: parallel current is identical in all branches

videoPackage.title: Power in circuits
videoPackage.transcript: We trace current through series and parallel paths, calculate power using consistent units, and distinguish energy from its rate of transfer.

units.title: Doppler effect and wave phenomena
units.why: Wave phenomena explain sound, measurement, communication and astronomical observations.
examples: A siren sounds higher as it approaches and lower as it recedes
Shorter wavelength at unchanged speed means higher frequency
misconceptions: source frequency changes because observer hears it

videoPackage.title: Waves in relative motion
videoPackage.transcript: We compare wavefront spacing in front of and behind a moving source, then connect frequency shifts to sound and astronomy.
